title: A capped overnight candidate queue

known_project_facts.project: A national equipment maintenance network deduplicates asset records across monthly service feeds; assets are not sites or product families.
known_project_facts.scale: 18 million rows; 600000 updates per month; batch window two hours; 64 GB RAM; CPU budget only. Some manufacturer serial numbers repeat across namespaces and refurbished units.
known_project_facts.current_pipeline: Exact serial and normalized site/name passes. A few common serial-like placeholders generate giant blocks. Engineers retain only the first 25 candidates per row by input order. Scores and thresholds were fitted before the cap.
known_project_facts.observations: Reported pair precision remains high, but technicians find duplicates omitted from the queue. A proposal adds broad embedding ANN retrieval plus a costly cross-encoder to every pair.
known_project_facts.constraints: Need bounded candidate/scoring workloads, stable replay and audit trails. No representative missed-match labels; equipment history must survive updates and correction.

explicitly_unknown: What are block-size, marginal pass coverage and cost distributions?
What recall loss does ordering/capping impose on source and asset slices?
What workload and replay guardrails make added retrieval practical?
task: Produce a defensible project-specific ER experiment/design recommendation using selectively retrieved Atlas knowledge if available. Do not implement ER or change production. Separate facts, assumptions, uncertainties, mechanisms and proposed evidence.
